project_specification.overview:
AutoForge Website Bridge is the integration layer that connects the autoforge.com SaaS website (built on the Gen-Ai boilerplate) to AutoForge build workers running on cloud VMs. It enables users to start builds from the web UI, stream real-time progress via WebSocket, receive packaged project artifacts on completion, and manage specs and project expansion -- all with multi-tenant isolation and Supabase JWT authentication. The bridge turns two separate systems (a static SaaS shell and a local coding agent) into a unified cloud build platform.
Built on the Gen-Ai SaaS boilerplate (React 18 + Vite + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Supabase Auth + Stripe), this project adds build orchestration, worker management, artifact delivery, and real-time streaming to the existing website infrastructure.

frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui and Radix UI
frontend.state_management: React hooks, context, and Supabase realtime subscriptions

backend.runtime: Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Edge Functions, Row-Level Security)
backend.database: Supabase Postgres (extends existing Gen-Ai boilerplate schema)
backend.billing: Stripe (subscriptions, one-time purchases, credit system -- already in boilerplate)
backend.worker_provider: Fly.io Machines API for ephemeral build worker VMs
backend.artifact_storage: Cloudflare R2 / AWS S3 for build artifact storage

communication.api: RESTful endpoints + Supabase Edge Functions + WebSocket for real-time streaming

prerequisites.environment_setup: - Node.js 18+ installed - npm package manager - Supabase project configured (Auth, Postgres, Edge Functions) - Stripe account with test and live API keys (already in boilerplate) - Fly.io account with API token for worker provisioning - Cloudflare R2 or AWS S3 bucket for artifact storage - Resend account for transactional email (already in boilerplate) - Gen-Ai boilerplate cloned as project base with autoforge.com branding applied - BUILD_JWT_SECRET for signing per-build auth tokens - PLATFORM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for managed (non-BYOK) builds

core_features.infrastructure: - System connects to Supabase Postgres and returns data from a test query - System applies database migrations creating builds, build_workers, and user_specs tables with all columns, indexes, and RLS policies - Data persists in Supabase Postgres across Edge Function restarts and redeployments - System contains no mock data patterns, in-memory stores, or hardcoded sample data - API endpoints query real Supabase Postgres via the Supabase client, not stubs
core_features.build_orchestrator: - POST /api/builds/start validates Supabase JWT, checks credit balance, consumes credit atomically, inserts a builds row with status 'queued', and returns build_id with WebSocket URL - Build orchestrator checks the build_workers table for an idle worker and assigns it to the build, updating worker status to 'assigned' and build status to 'provisioning' - When no idle worker is available, build orchestrator provisions a new Fly.io Machine via the Machines API with the correct Docker image, environment variables, and resource allocation - Build orchestrator configures the assigned worker by writing app_spec.txt, setting environment variables (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, BUILD_AUTH_TOKEN, BUILD_CALLBACK_URL), and starting the AutoForge process - Build orchestrator manages a priority queue for builds when all workers are busy, returning queue position to the user - Build orchestrator tears down worker VMs within 10 minutes of build completion by stopping and destroying the Fly Machine
core_features.websocket_proxy: - WebSocket endpoint at /api/builds/{build_id}/ws accepts a Supabase JWT, validates ownership, looks up the worker URL from the builds table, and opens a proxied WebSocket connection to the worker - Proxy translates AutoForge internal event format (progress, agent_status, log, agent_update) into the SaaS build_progress format with build_id, timestamp, and structured data payload - Proxy persists key events back to the builds table: features_completed, features_total, progress_percentage, current_phase, and status transitions - Proxy buffers the last 100 events per build and replays missed events on client reconnection
core_features.artifact_delivery: - On build completion, worker packages project files into a tar.gz archive excluding node_modules, .git, venv, __pycache__, and .autoforge directories - System uploads the archive and any generated reports (spec-analysis.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, qa-report.md) to cloud storage at builds/{user_id}/{build_id}/ path - System generates pre-signed download URLs with 7-day expiry and writes artifact_url, artifact_size_bytes, and artifact_expires_at to the builds table - GET /api/builds/{build_id}/download validates Supabase JWT, confirms ownership, and returns a 302 redirect to the pre-signed cloud storage URL - GET /api/builds/{build_id}/reports returns rendered spec_analysis_md, architecture_md, and qa_report_md from the builds table
core_features.multi_tenant_isolation: - Each build runs on a separate Fly.io Machine with its own ephemeral filesystem at /builds/{build_id}/, destroyed after completion - Workers run on a private network and are only reachable through the WebSocket proxy -- no direct inbound access from the internet - All Supabase tables (builds, build_workers, user_specs) enforce Row-Level Security policies so users can only access their own data - BYOK API keys are decrypted from the byok_keys table only at worker provisioning time and injected via environment variable -- never written to disk on the worker - Platform Anthropic API key is injected via environment variable and never exposed in client-side code or logs
core_features.authentication_bridge: - All /api/builds/* endpoints validate the Supabase JWT from the Authorization header and extract user_id for database queries - On worker provisioning, the orchestrator generates a short-lived BUILD_AUTH_TOKEN JWT (signed with BUILD_JWT_SECRET) with claims containing build_id, user_id, and expiry set to build duration plus 1 hour - The WebSocket proxy includes the BUILD_AUTH_TOKEN in the X-Build-Token header when forwarding requests to the worker - The callback and heartbeat endpoints validate the X-Build-Token header from workers to ensure only the assigned worker can report on a build
core_features.build_callbacks: - POST /api/builds/{build_id}/callback accepts events (started, phase_change, progress, completed, failed, crashed) with X-Build-Token validation - On 'completed' callback, system updates build status, records duration_minutes, triggers artifact packaging, and sends completion email via Resend - On 'failed' callback, system updates build status with error_message, packages any completed work, and triggers auto-refund if retry_count exceeds max_retries - On 'crashed' callback (or heartbeat timeout), system checks retry_count against max_retries, re-provisions worker preserving features.db if retries remain, or marks build as failed with refund
core_features.worker_health_monitoring: - POST /api/builds/{build_id}/heartbeat accepts periodic health reports (cpu_percent, memory_percent, disk_percent, agent_pid, active_agents) with X-Build-Token validation, updating last_heartbeat_at on the build_workers table - Background job checks all running workers every 60 seconds and marks any worker with no heartbeat for 90 seconds as unhealthy - Workers with no heartbeat for 180 seconds are treated as crashed, triggering the crash recovery flow (retry or fail with refund) - Builds running longer than BUILD_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MINUTES (default 180) are automatically terminated with a timeout error and partial artifact packaging - Admin dashboard extension displays worker pool utilization, unhealthy workers, and builds exceeding time limits
core_features.build_dashboard: - /builds/new page displays a multi-step wizard: Step 1 (app spec input with paste/upload/AI-chat options), Step 2 (boilerplate selection grid), Step 3 (style picker with preview), Step 4 (build config: credit type, BYOK toggle, YOLO mode, model selection), Step 5 (review summary with cost and Start Build button) - /builds/{id} page displays real-time build view with progress bar (features completed/total), phase indicator (Spec Analysis to Testing), agent cards with mascot names and current feature, scrolling log stream with feature-level filtering, mini kanban board (Pending/In Progress/Done), and Pause/Resume/Cancel action buttons - /builds/{id}/results page displays download button (tar.gz with 7-day link), rendered spec analysis and architecture reports, QA report with test results, and build metrics (duration, tokens, features completed/failed) - /builds page displays build history list with status badges, date, features total/passing, credits used, and filters for status and date range - /dashboard page shows overview cards for active builds, recent builds, and credit balance with quick-action links
core_features.spec_creation_chat: - user_specs table stores saved specifications with id, user_id, name, content (app_spec.txt), and chat_history (JSONB) with RLS policies enforcing user-scoped access - WebSocket endpoint at /api/specs/chat/ws accepts Supabase JWT and streams an AI-assisted spec creation conversation using the Anthropic Messages API with the spec creation system prompt template - Spec creation uses claude-sonnet-4-6 model directly from the web app server (no build worker needed) and returns a structured app_spec.txt on completion - /specs page displays list of saved specs with name, creation date, edit/delete/duplicate actions, and empty state with CTA - /specs/new page provides chat-based spec creation interface with streaming response display - /specs/{id}/edit page provides text editor for manual spec editing plus chat-based refinement option
core_features.project_expand_assistant: - POST /api/builds/{build_id}/expand validates Supabase JWT, confirms build ownership and completed status, deducts 1 additional credit, provisions a worker with the original project files downloaded from cloud storage, and returns expansion_build_id with WebSocket URL - POST /api/builds/{build_id}/assistant/message accepts a message string and optional conversation_id, downloads project files to a temporary directory, and streams a Claude API response with file context for read-only project Q&A - /builds/{id}/results page includes "Add Features" button that triggers the expand flow and "Ask About This Project" chat panel for the assistant
core_features.build_admin: - Admin builds page at /admin/builds displays all builds across all users with columns for status, user email, worker ID, duration, credits consumed, and action buttons for refund and force-terminate - Admin workers page at /admin/workers displays worker pool table with status, region, current build, last heartbeat, and terminate button - POST /api/admin/builds/{id}/refund performs manual credit refund for a failed or cancelled build (admin only) - POST /api/admin/workers/{id}/terminate force-terminates a worker VM and marks the associated build as failed (admin only) - Admin routes are protected with role-based access from the Gen-Ai boilerplate's admin system

tables.builds: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table for central build tracking - id (UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()) - user_id (UUID NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY -> auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE) - project_name (TEXT NOT NULL) - credit_type (TEXT NOT NULL) - is_byok (BOOLEAN DEFAULT false) - worker_id (TEXT, worker VM identifier) - worker_url (TEXT, internal URL to worker's AutoForge API) - worker_region (TEXT, deployment region) - app_spec (TEXT NOT NULL, full app_spec.txt content) - boilerplate_id (TEXT) - style_id (TEXT) - custom_colors (JSONB) - yolo_mode (BOOLEAN DEFAULT false) - model (TEXT DEFAULT 'claude-sonnet-4-6') - max_concurrency (INTEGER DEFAULT 3) - batch_size (INTEGER DEFAULT 3) - anthropic_api_key_encrypted (BYTEA, re-encrypted BYOK key for transit) - status (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued', CHECK IN ('queued', 'provisioning', 'initializing', 'building', 'testing', 'packaging', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'refunded')) - features_total (INTEGER DEFAULT 0) - features_completed (INTEGER DEFAULT 0) - features_failed (INTEGER DEFAULT 0) - current_phase (TEXT) - progress_percentage (NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 0) - artifact_url (TEXT, cloud storage URL for packaged project) - artifact_size_bytes (BIGINT) - artifact_expires_at (TIMESTAMPTZ, pre-signed URL expiry) - spec_analysis_md (TEXT) - architecture_md (TEXT) - qa_report_md (TEXT) - queued_at (TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()) - started_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) - completed_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) - duration_minutes (INTEGER) - error_message (TEXT) - retry_count (INTEGER DEFAULT 0) - max_retries (INTEGER DEFAULT 2) - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) INDEX: idx_builds_user ON builds(user_id, created_at DESC) INDEX: idx_builds_status ON builds(status) WHERE status IN ('queued', 'provisioning', 'building') INDEX: idx_builds_worker ON builds(worker_id) WHERE worker_id IS NOT NULL RLS: Users can SELECT only their own rows (auth.uid() = user_id)
tables.build_workers: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table for worker VM pool tracking - id (TEXT PRIMARY KEY, VM identifier from cloud provider) - provider (TEXT NOT NULL, 'fly' or 'gcp' or 'aws') - region (TEXT NOT NULL) - status (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'idle', CHECK IN ('idle', 'provisioning', 'assigned', 'running', 'draining', 'terminated')) - current_build_id (UUID, FOREIGN KEY -> builds(id)) - ip_address (TEXT) - internal_url (TEXT, private network URL) - machine_type (TEXT, e.g. 'shared-cpu-4x') - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()) - last_heartbeat_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) - terminated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) INDEX: idx_build_workers_status ON build_workers(status) WHERE status IN ('idle', 'assigned', 'running')
tables.user_specs: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table for saved app specifications - id (UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()) - user_id (UUID NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY -> auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE) - name (TEXT NOT NULL) - content (TEXT NOT NULL, app_spec.txt content) - chat_history (JSONB, conversation context for refinement) - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) INDEX: idx_user_specs_user_id ON user_specs(user_id) RLS: Users can full CRUD on their own rows (auth.uid() = user_id)

api_endpoints_summary.build_lifecycle: - GET /api/builds (list user's builds with pagination, status filter, date range) - POST /api/builds/start (validate JWT, check credits, consume credit, create build, assign worker, return build_id + ws_url) - GET /api/builds/{id} (get build details including progress, worker info, and timing) - POST /api/builds/{id}/cancel (cancel build, refund credit if not yet started) - POST /api/builds/{id}/pause (pause active build via worker API) - POST /api/builds/{id}/resume (resume paused build via worker API) - WS /api/builds/{id}/ws (real-time progress streaming via WebSocket proxy) - GET /api/builds/{id}/download (302 redirect to pre-signed artifact URL) - GET /api/builds/{id}/reports (spec analysis, architecture, QA report content) - POST /api/builds/{id}/expand (start expansion build with original project files) - POST /api/builds/{id}/assistant/message (project Q&A chat with streamed response)
api_endpoints_summary.build_callbacks: - POST /api/builds/{id}/callback (worker lifecycle events: started, phase_change, progress, completed, failed, crashed) - POST /api/builds/{id}/heartbeat (worker health reports with CPU, memory, disk metrics)
api_endpoints_summary.spec_management: - GET /api/specs (list user's saved specs with pagination) - POST /api/specs (create new spec) - GET /api/specs/{id} (get spec content and chat history) - PATCH /api/specs/{id} (update spec name or content) - DELETE /api/specs/{id} (delete spec) - WS /api/specs/chat/ws (AI-assisted spec creation via streaming chat)
api_endpoints_summary.build_admin: - GET /api/admin/builds (list all builds with filters -- admin only) - GET /api/admin/workers (worker pool status and health -- admin only) - POST /api/admin/builds/{id}/refund (manual credit refund -- admin only) - POST /api/admin/workers/{id}/terminate (force terminate worker -- admin only)

ui_layout.main_structure: - Header with navigation and user menu (from Gen-Ai boilerplate) - Sidebar with navigation links: Dashboard, New Build, Builds, Specs, Settings (collapsible on mobile) - Main content area for current page
ui_layout.pages: - /dashboard: Active builds overview, recent builds, credit balance, quick actions - /builds/new: Multi-step new build wizard (spec, boilerplate, style, config, review) - /builds: Build history list with status badges, filters, search - /builds/{id}: Live build view with progress, logs, agents, kanban, actions - /builds/{id}/results: Completed build with download, reports, metrics, expand, assistant - /specs: Saved specs list with CRUD actions - /specs/new: Chat-based spec creation - /specs/{id}/edit: Spec editor with chat refinement - /admin/builds: All builds admin view (admin only) - /admin/workers: Worker pool management (admin only)

design_system.color_palette: NOTE: Inherits Gen-Ai boilerplate defaults with AutoForge branding - Primary: #6366F1 (indigo -- AutoForge brand) - Secondary: #8B5CF6 (violet -- accent) - Background: #FFFFFF (light), #0F172A (dark) - Text: #1E293B (light), #E2E8F0 (dark) - Error: #EF4444 - Success: #10B981 - Warning: #F59E0B - Muted: #64748B
design_system.typography: - Font family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif - Headings: font-bold - Body: font-normal - Code: JetBrains Mono, monospace
design_system.spacing: - Base unit: 4px (Tailwind default) - Card padding: p-6 (24px) - Section gap: gap-8 (32px) - Form field gap: gap-4 (16px) - Page max-width: max-w-7xl (1280px) centered
design_system.components: - Use shadcn/ui and Radix UI components from boilerplate - Consistent border-radius: rounded-lg (8px) - Consistent shadow: shadow-sm for cards, shadow-lg for modals - Button variants: default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link

ui_ux_standards.banned_patterns: - alert(), confirm(), prompt() -- Use shadcn/ui Dialog and Toast instead - Text-only empty states -- Use EmptyState component with icon + CTA - Loading states that just say "Loading..." -- Use Skeleton components from shadcn/ui - Delete without confirmation -- Always use AlertDialog (shadcn/ui ConfirmModal equivalent) - Raw timestamps -- Format as relative time using date-fns or similar - Hardcoded API keys in source code -- Always use environment variables - Inline styles -- Tailwind utility classes only
ui_ux_standards.required_components: - Dialog (Modal), AlertDialog (ConfirmModal), Toast notification system - Skeleton loader, EmptyState with icon and CTA, ErrorBoundary - Button with loading spinner state, Avatar with fallback initials - Badge for status indicators (queued, building, completed, failed) - Progress bar for build progress and provisioning status
ui_ux_standards.page_patterns: - List View -> Detail View (read-only) -> Edit View - Never open directly into edit mode from a list - Separate view and edit concerns - Wizard flows use multi-step modal with back/next navigation and progress indicator
ui_ux_standards.feedback_protocol: - Success: toast + navigate. Error: toast + stay + keep data. - Delete: confirm dialog -> loading -> toast + redirect - Build start: confirm credit deduction -> loading -> redirect to live build view - Long operations (provisioning, packaging): real-time status messages via WebSocket
ui_ux_standards.polish_requirements: - Relative dates, text truncation, back navigation, hover states, focus states - Autofocus first input in forms, search/filter on lists with 5+ items - Retry action on every error state, loading skeletons for async data
ui_ux_standards.accessibility_basics: - Focus rings on interactive elements, Escape closes dialogs - aria-labels on icon-only buttons, labels on all form inputs - Keyboard navigation through wizard steps

coding_standards.architecture: - Gen-Ai boilerplate conventions for all web platform code - One component per file, feature folders for grouping - Service layer: Supabase client calls in services/hooks, not UI components - TypeScript interfaces for all data types, no 'any' - Environment variables for all secrets and configuration - Edge Functions for server-side operations requiring secrets (Fly.io API token, BUILD_JWT_SECRET)
coding_standards.routing: - Public routes: none (all bridge features require authentication) - Protected routes: dashboard, builds, specs, settings (Supabase auth guard from boilerplate) - Admin routes: admin builds, admin workers (role-based access from boilerplate) - 404 catch-all route
coding_standards.error_handling: - ErrorBoundary wraps entire app (already in boilerplate) - User-friendly error messages, not raw errors - Retry action on every error state - Graceful degradation when Fly.io API is unreachable - Callback and heartbeat endpoints return 200 even on internal errors to prevent retry flooding - WebSocket proxy handles disconnection and reconnection gracefully with event replay
coding_standards.security: - Supabase JWT validation on all API endpoints - Per-build BUILD_AUTH_TOKEN JWTs for worker-to-web-app communication - BYOK keys decrypted only at provisioning time, injected via env var, never written to disk - Workers on private network, no direct inbound access - Workers destroyed within 10 minutes of build completion - Stripe webhook signature verification on all webhook handlers (from boilerplate) - Admin routes use server-side role verification, not just frontend guards

key_interactions.start_build_flow: 1. User navigates to /builds/new 2. User enters app spec (paste, upload, or AI-chat creation) 3. User selects boilerplate and style 4. User configures build (credit type, BYOK, YOLO, model) 5. User reviews summary and clicks Start Build 6. System validates JWT, checks credit balance, consumes credit 7. System creates builds row, assigns or provisions worker 8. User is redirected to /builds/{id} live view 9. WebSocket proxy streams real-time progress, logs, and agent state 10. Build completes: artifact packaged, email sent, results page available
key_interactions.build_failure_and_recovery_flow: 1. Worker process crashes or heartbeat times out (180s) 2. Orchestrator detects failure via missing heartbeat or crash callback 3. If retry_count < max_retries: re-provision worker, copy features.db, restart agent 4. WebSocket notifies user of retry with status update 5. If max retries exceeded: mark build as failed, package completed work 6. System triggers auto-refund and sends failure notification email 7. User sees failed build with partial download and error details
key_interactions.spec_creation_flow: 1. User navigates to /specs/new 2. Chat interface opens with AI-assisted spec creation 3. User describes their app idea through conversation 4. Claude generates structured app_spec.txt 5. User reviews and optionally refines the spec 6. User saves spec to user_specs table 7. Saved spec is available in the new build wizard's spec selection step

step.title: Database Schema and Infrastructure
step.tasks: - Create builds, build_workers, and user_specs tables in Supabase with all columns, constraints, and indexes - Apply Row-Level Security policies on all new tables - Verify data persistence across Edge Function restarts - Create TypeScript interfaces for all database entities

step.title: Authentication Bridge and Build Start API
step.tasks: - Implement Supabase JWT validation middleware for /api/builds/* routes - Implement BUILD_AUTH_TOKEN generation (JWT signing with BUILD_JWT_SECRET) - Build POST /api/builds/start endpoint with credit validation and atomic consumption - Build GET /api/builds and GET /api/builds/{id} endpoints

step.title: Build Orchestrator and Worker Provisioning
step.tasks: - Implement Fly.io Machines API integration (create, configure, start, stop, destroy) - Build worker assignment logic (check pool, provision new, queue management) - Implement worker configuration (write app_spec, set env vars, start AutoForge) - Build worker teardown logic (stop, destroy after grace period)

step.title: WebSocket Proxy and Real-Time Streaming
step.tasks: - Build WebSocket endpoint at /api/builds/{id}/ws with JWT validation - Implement proxy connection to worker WebSocket with BUILD_AUTH_TOKEN - Implement event format translation (AutoForge internal to SaaS format) - Implement event persistence (update builds table on progress/status changes) - Implement event buffering and replay on reconnection

step.title: Build Callbacks and Health Monitoring
step.tasks: - Build POST /api/builds/{id}/callback endpoint with token validation - Build POST /api/builds/{id}/heartbeat endpoint with token validation - Implement crash recovery flow (retry logic, features.db preservation) - Implement timeout enforcement (BUILD_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MINUTES) - Build background health check job (60-second interval)

step.title: Artifact Delivery
step.tasks: - Implement artifact packaging on worker (tar.gz with exclusions) - Implement cloud storage upload (R2/S3) with report files - Implement pre-signed URL generation with 7-day expiry - Build GET /api/builds/{id}/download endpoint - Build GET /api/builds/{id}/reports endpoint - Send completion email via Resend with download link

step.title: Build Dashboard UI
step.tasks: - Build /builds/new multi-step wizard (spec, boilerplate, style, config, review) - Build /builds/{id} live build view (progress, logs, agents, kanban, actions) - Build /builds/{id}/results page (download, reports, metrics) - Build /builds history list with status badges and filters - Build /dashboard overview cards (active builds, recent builds, credits)

step.title: Spec Management
step.tasks: - Build spec creation chat WebSocket with Anthropic Messages API - Build /specs list page with CRUD actions - Build /specs/new chat-based creation interface - Build /specs/{id}/edit page with text editor and chat refinement - Wire saved specs into the new build wizard

step.title: Project Expand and Assistant
step.tasks: - Build POST /api/builds/{id}/expand endpoint (re-provision worker with existing files) - Build POST /api/builds/{id}/assistant/message endpoint (Claude API with file context) - Add "Add Features" button and "Ask About This Project" chat panel to results page

step.title: Admin and Multi-Tenant Isolation
step.tasks: - Build /admin/builds page with all-builds table and action buttons - Build /admin/workers page with pool status and terminate button - Build POST /api/admin/builds/{id}/refund endpoint - Build POST /api/admin/workers/{id}/terminate endpoint - Verify multi-tenant isolation: RLS policies, private networking, ephemeral filesystems - Verify BYOK key handling: decrypt only at provisioning, inject via env var

success_criteria.functionality: - User can start a build from the web UI and see real-time progress via WebSocket - Build orchestrator provisions, configures, and tears down workers automatically - Completed builds produce downloadable project archives with reports - Failed builds retry automatically and refund credits when retries are exhausted - Worker health monitoring detects crashes and timeouts within 180 seconds - Spec creation chat generates valid app_spec.txt without needing a build worker - Project expand correctly re-provisions a worker with the original project files - Multi-tenant isolation ensures users cannot access other users' builds, workers, or data - BYOK keys are never exposed in logs, client-side code, or written to worker disk
success_criteria.user_experience: - Build wizard guides users through spec, boilerplate, style, and config selection - Live build view provides real-time feedback with progress bar, agent cards, and log stream - Build results page clearly presents download, reports, and expansion options - All pages responsive on mobile (375px), tablet (768px), desktop (1920px) - All actions provide immediate visual feedback via toasts and status updates - Reconnecting to a live build replays missed events seamlessly
success_criteria.technical_quality: - Zero console errors in browser - All Supabase tables protected by Row-Level Security policies - API keys never exposed in client-side code - Webhook and callback handlers validate auth tokens on every request - WebSocket proxy handles disconnection gracefully with event buffering - TypeScript strict mode with no 'any' types - All Edge Functions include proper error handling and rollback logic
